ShortDescription.Value: Progressive job seeking for small cities

Publish.LongDescription:
Mod Support: Support the mod's continued development by clicking the Like button.
Supported/recommended mods: Progression Control and Hard Mode Continued.
Unsupported mods: Code mods that override the same game systems are generally incompatible. Check the Override folder on GitHub for the systems overridden by this mod.
From version 1.4.22 mod saves data directly in the savegame.
- Added new tab showing citizens who are shopping (buying resource, not leasure shopping) - Icons: status, age, wealth, family size. - Includes shopping duration countdown. - New icon design for the main tabs. - Implemented small city shopping basics: allowing more detailed individual shopping simulation in smaller cities. - Introduced individual shopping durations. Instead of leaving immediately after arriving, citizens can remain at commercial buildings for a configurable amount of time. - Added a Normal Shopping setting that gradually restores the game's original shopping behavior as the city grows. - Shopping duration takes citizens' daily schedules into account, including their next work, school, or sleep period. - Added Minimum Shopping Duration and Maximum Shopping Duration settings to control how much of their available time citizens spend shopping. - Leisure and Shopping tab lists are now sorted by full name - Fixed possible crash when viewing tabs when citizens leaving - Fixed localizationID BitulaMod.LIFEPATH_None not found warning - Fixed end of leisure check applies to vanilla (not checking settings) - Major code restructure into smallcity template objects - see github smallcity folder
Small City Jobs is designed to make employment and leisure behaviour feel more natural in small towns and villages.
In the vanilla game, citizens can be surprisingly reluctant to take available jobs when only a small number of suitable positions exist. This works reasonably well in large cities with hundreds of vacancies, but can cause unrealistic behaviour in small settlements, where even a handful of open jobs may represent a significant part of the local economy.
The goal of this mod is not to replace the vanilla simulation, but to make some of its systems scale better with city size.
In smaller cities, citizens are more willing to take available jobs, accept reasonable alternatives, and look for better employment opportunities. The mod also reduces situations where adults leave employment or choose studying simply because the local job market is small, including cases where they would otherwise travel outside the city to study despite suitable work being available.
As the population grows, these employment adjustments gradually fade and the game returns toward its original behaviour.
The mod also improves leisure behaviour. In the vanilla game, the chance for citizens to seek leisure can be very low, which is especially noticeable in smaller cities where parks, cinemas and other leisure locations may remain unusually empty. The optional Normal Leisure setting makes citizens seek leisure at a more natural frequency while preserving the existing leisure system and provider requirements.
The mod adds UI and Life Path improvements for both employment and leisure. These expose more of what citizens are doing and why, including job decisions, leisure choices, failed searches, unavailable services, and the locations citizens decide to visit.
The overall aim is to make villages and small towns feel more active and believable without making employment artificially easy or replacing the game's existing simulation in larger cities.
The progression of the employment changes and the Normal Leisure behaviour can be configured in the game options.
Several vanilla issues are also addressed, some I also posted in official bugfix forum.
Detailed mechanics, settings and individual changes are documented in the forum discussion.
